title: Tonsured and oiled and gelded
html_source:
Stephen here uses livestock terminology to describe being overweight, because he struggles with the word ‘fat’. It may represent the bodily to him.

Also consider the hair motif and comparison to Buck Mulligan’s ‘light and untonsored hair’ in a narrative section at the beginning of telemachus.

anchor.prefix: monstrance, basiliskeyed. Get down, bald poll! A choir gives back menace and echo, assisting about the altar's horns, the snorted Latin of jackpriests moving burly in their albs,
anchor.suffix:
, fat with the fat of kidneys of wheat. 

 And at the same instant perhaps a priest round the corner is elevating it. Dringdring! And two streets off another locking it into a pyx.
